title: Electric Internals
subtitle: Durable Proxy, Durable State, StreamDB and StreamFS
throughline: One durable stream dressed up four ways: a resumable proxy, typed state, a reactive database, and a filesystem.

chapters.title: Durable Proxy
chapters.blurb: A resumable proxy persists an AI provider's streaming response into Durable Streams and hands clients a read URL they can reconnect to.

story.title: Durable Proxy
story.subtitle: Durable Proxy, Durable State, StreamDB and StreamFS

steps.title: Durable Proxy
steps.narration: **Durable Proxy** puts resumable streaming in front of existing AI APIs with `@durable-streams/proxy`.
steps.say: Streaming from an A I provider is fragile. Refresh the page, drop the connection, and the answer is gone. The durable proxy fixes that.
steps.coverSubtitle: Resumable streaming in front of any AI provider

steps.title: Start the proxy server
steps.narration: `createProxyServer({ port, durableStreamsUrl, jwtSecret, allowlist })` stands up a relay that sits between your client and an upstream provider.
steps.say: You start with create proxy server. You give it a port, the durable streams U R L, a J W T secret, and an allowlist of providers it may reach.

steps.title: Call durableFetch like fetch
steps.narration: On the client, `createDurableFetch({ proxyUrl, proxyAuthorization, autoResume, storage })` returns a `durableFetch` you call exactly like `fetch`.
steps.say: On the client, create durable fetch returns a durable fetch. You call it just like the normal fetch, but every request now flows through the proxy.

steps.title: Forward to the provider
steps.narration: The proxy forwards the request to an upstream provider on the `allowlist`, such as `api.openai.com` or `api.anthropic.com`.
steps.say: The proxy forwards your request to the upstream provider, the one you allowlisted, and the provider begins streaming its response back token by token.

steps.title: Persist into Durable Streams
steps.narration: As tokens arrive, the proxy persists the streaming response into **Durable Streams** at `durableStreamsUrl` instead of letting it evaporate.
steps.say: Here is the trick. As those tokens arrive, the proxy persists the streaming response into durable streams. The answer is now saved, not just passing through.

steps.title: Return a durable read URL
steps.narration: The proxy returns a **durable read URL** backed by the persisted stream, so the client reads the answer from storage rather than the live socket.
steps.say: The proxy hands back a durable read U R L. The client reads the answer from that saved stream, the very same tokens, now served from durable storage.

steps.title: Resume with requestId
steps.narration: A `requestId` like `conversation-123` lets the client resume the *same* durable stream across refreshes and reconnects, with `autoResume` reattaching automatically.
steps.say: And because each call carries a request I D, the client can resume the same durable stream across refreshes and reconnects. Close the tab, come back, and the answer is still streaming where you left it.

chapters.title: Durable State
chapters.blurb: Typed insert, update and delete events ride one JSON stream, with snapshot and reset control markers, and MaterializedState folds them into a key-value store.

story.title: Durable State
story.subtitle: Durable Proxy, Durable State, StreamDB and StreamFS

steps.title: Durable State
steps.narration: **Durable State** adds typed `insert`, `update`, and `delete` events on top of Durable Streams with `@durable-streams/state`.
steps.say: A raw stream is just bytes. Durable state dresses those bytes up as structured database changes, so a stream starts to behave like a table.
steps.coverSubtitle: Structured CRUD on top of a raw stream

steps.title: Append to a JSON stream
steps.narration: Durable State uses JSON streams with `Content-Type: application/json`. A producer appends events; clients materialize state by applying them in order.
steps.say: It runs over a J S O N stream. A producer appends events one after another, and any reader rebuilds state by applying those events in order.

steps.title: Typed change events
steps.narration: A **change event** carries `{ type, key, value, old_value? }` and an `headers.operation` of `insert`, `update`, or `delete`.
steps.say: Most events are change events. Each one names a type, a key, and a value, and its headers carry an operation: insert, update, or delete. That is create, read, update, delete over a stream.

steps.title: Many types, one stream
steps.narration: The `type` field routes each event to the right collection, so `user`, `message`, and `reaction` events can interleave in one stream and still process in order.
steps.say: Multiple entity types share the same stream. Users, messages, reactions, all interleaved. The type field routes each event to the right place, so one stream can model a whole chat room.

steps.title: Snapshot and reset control
steps.narration: **Control events** set `headers.control` instead of an operation: `snapshot-start` and `snapshot-end` bound a full state dump, while `reset` tells clients to clear and restart.
steps.say: Separate from data, control events manage the stream. Snapshot start and snapshot end bound a full dump of current state. Reset tells every client to clear what it has and start over.

steps.title: Fold into MaterializedState
steps.narration: `MaterializedState` is an in-memory key-value store. `state.apply(event)` folds each change in; `get(type, key)` and `getType(type)` read it back.
steps.say: A materialized state is the simplest consumer. It is an in-memory key-value store. You call apply for each event, and it folds the changes into a map from type and key to the latest value.

steps.title: Bytes, CRUD, then apps
steps.narration: The pattern layers: **Durable Streams** for bytes, the **State Protocol** for CRUD, and application protocols on top. A `reset` re-snapshots cleanly.
steps.say: So the layering is clear. Durable streams deliver bytes. The state protocol turns those bytes into create, read, update, delete. And application protocols build on top. When a reset arrives, the materialized state clears and the next snapshot rebuilds it.

chapters.title: StreamDB
chapters.blurb: A typed schema turns a stream into a reactive database with live queries and optimistic actions that update locally before persisting.

story.title: StreamDB
story.subtitle: Durable Proxy, Durable State, StreamDB and StreamFS

steps.title: StreamDB
steps.narration: **StreamDB** is a type-safe reactive database in a durable stream, built on Durable State and `@tanstack/db`.
steps.say: Now we go further. Stream D B turns that same stream into a type-safe reactive database, with live queries and optimistic updates.
steps.coverSubtitle: A type-safe reactive database in a stream

steps.title: Define a typed schema
steps.narration: `createStateSchema({ users: { schema, type, primaryKey } })` maps each entity type to any Standard Schema validator, like Zod, Valibot, or ArkType.
steps.say: First you define a state schema. Create state schema maps each collection to a type, a primary key, and a validator. Any standard schema works, whether that is Zod, Valibot, or Ark Type.

steps.title: Connect to a stream
steps.narration: `createStreamDB({ streamOptions: { url, contentType }, state, actions })` connects the schema to a Durable Stream and creates a reactive, stream-backed database.
steps.say: Then create stream D B connects that schema to a durable stream. You pass stream options with a U R L and a content type, and you get back a reactive, stream-backed database.

steps.title: Preload and stay live
steps.narration: `db.preload()` reads the stream from the beginning, materializes current state, and then stays connected for live updates.
steps.say: Calling preload reads the stream from the very beginning, materializes the current state, and then stays connected so new changes keep flowing in.

steps.title: Reactive live queries
steps.narration: Collections are TanStack DB collections. `useLiveQuery` runs filters, joins, and counts that update incrementally through differential dataflow.
steps.say: Now you query with use live query. These are Tan Stack D B collections, so you can filter, join, and count. And thanks to differential dataflow, every query updates incrementally, never recomputing from scratch.

steps.title: Optimistic actions
steps.narration: An action's `onMutate` updates local state immediately; `mutationFn` then persists to the stream with a `crypto.randomUUID()` txid.
steps.say: Mutations feel instant. An action's on mutate updates the local collection right away, so the U I responds immediately. Then the mutation function persists the change to the stream, stamped with a fresh transaction I D.

steps.title: Confirm and roll back
steps.narration: `db.utils.awaitTxId(txid, ms)` waits for the change to land; if the server rejects it, TanStack DB rolls back the optimistic update. `db.close()` tears it down.
steps.say: To confirm, await transaction I D waits for that change to land in the stream. If the server rejects it, Tan Stack D B rolls the optimistic update back. And when you are done, close tears the whole thing down cleanly.

chapters.title: StreamFS
chapters.blurb: A shared filesystem for AI agents stores metadata and content in separate streams, with file operations and chokidar-style watch events over eventual consistency.

story.title: StreamFS
story.subtitle: Durable Proxy, Durable State, StreamDB and StreamFS

steps.title: StreamFS
steps.narration: **StreamFS** is a shared filesystem for AI agents, with files, directories, and watch-based sync over Durable Streams.
steps.say: Same stream, one more disguise. Stream F S gives A I agents a shared filesystem, with files, directories, and watchers, all backed by durable streams.
steps.coverSubtitle: A shared filesystem for AI agents

steps.title: Initialize the filesystem
steps.narration: `new StreamFilesystem({ baseUrl, streamPrefix })` then `fs.initialize()` brings up a filesystem rooted at a stream prefix.
steps.say: You construct a stream filesystem with a base U R L and a stream prefix, then call initialize. From here, an agent works with ordinary file operations.

steps.title: Metadata in one stream
steps.narration: StreamFS keeps directory structure and file metadata in a single **metadata stream** at `/_metadata`.
steps.say: Underneath, it splits state into two kinds of streams. Directory structure and file metadata live in one metadata stream.

steps.title: Content in its own streams
steps.narration: Each file's bytes live in a **content stream** at `/_content/{id}`, separate from metadata so the two can replay independently.
steps.say: File contents live separately, in content streams, one per file. Keeping bytes apart from metadata means each can be replayed on its own for durable recovery.

steps.title: Create and read files
steps.narration: `createFile('/notes.md', ...)` writes both streams; `readTextFile('/notes.md')` reads the content back, alongside `mkdir`, `list`, `move`, and `stat`.
steps.say: Create file writes a new file across both streams. Read text file reads its contents back. And the usual operations are all here too: make directory, list, move, and stat.

steps.title: Watch for changes
steps.narration: `fs.watch({ path, recursive })` emits chokidar-style events: `add`, `change`, `unlink`, `addDir`, and `unlinkDir`, so other agents react to edits live.
steps.say: To stay in sync, an agent arms a watcher over a path. It emits chokidar-style events: add, change, unlink, and their directory cousins. When one agent edits a file, the others hear about it.

steps.title: Stale-write detection
steps.narration: Because agents share state under eventual consistency, a conflicting write throws `PreconditionFailedError`, and durable replay rebuilds the tree from `/_metadata` and `/_content`.
steps.say: Many agents share this filesystem under eventual consistency, so conflicts happen. A stale write raises a precondition failed error. And because everything is durable, the whole tree can be replayed from its metadata and content streams.

chapters.title: One Stream, Four Faces
chapters.blurb: The proxy, state, database and filesystem are all the same Durable Streams primitive, layered up from bytes to CRUD to whole applications.

story.title: One Stream, Four Faces
story.subtitle: Durable Proxy, Durable State, StreamDB and StreamFS

steps.title: One Stream, Four Faces
steps.narration: Four packages, one foundation: the **Durable Streams** primitive underneath the proxy, state, database, and filesystem.
steps.say: We have seen four packages. Now let us step back and see the one thing they all share underneath.
steps.coverSubtitle: The same primitive, dressed four ways

steps.title: The shared primitive
steps.narration: At the base sits **Durable Streams**: reliable, resumable, replayable byte delivery. Every other package is a costume worn over it.
steps.say: At the very bottom is durable streams: reliable, resumable, replayable byte delivery. Everything else is a costume worn over this one primitive.

steps.title: Face one: the proxy
steps.narration: The **Durable Proxy** dresses the stream as resumable AI streaming, persisting upstream responses and handing back a `requestId`-resumable read URL.
steps.say: The first face is the durable proxy. It dresses the stream as resumable A I streaming, saving an upstream answer and letting clients reconnect by request I D.

steps.title: Face two: typed state
steps.narration: **Durable State** dresses the same bytes as typed `insert`, `update`, and `delete` events, folded into `MaterializedState`.
steps.say: The second face is durable state. It dresses the same bytes as typed insert, update, and delete events, which a materialized state folds into a key-value store.

steps.title: Face three: the database
steps.narration: **StreamDB** layers on Durable State to become a reactive database with `useLiveQuery` and optimistic actions over the stream.
steps.say: The third face is stream D B. It builds on durable state to become a reactive database, with live queries and optimistic actions running over the very same stream.

steps.title: Face four: the filesystem
steps.narration: **StreamFS** dresses streams as a shared filesystem, with metadata and content streams and chokidar-style `watch` events for agents.
steps.say: The fourth face is stream F S. It dresses streams as a shared filesystem, with metadata and content streams and live watch events for collaborating agents.

steps.title: Bytes, CRUD, applications
steps.narration: From one resumable stream rise four faces — proxy, state, database, filesystem — layering **bytes** into **CRUD** into whole **applications** for AI agents and UIs.
steps.say: So there it is. One resumable stream of bytes, layered into structured C R U D, layered into whole applications. A proxy, typed state, a database, and a filesystem, all the same durable stream wearing four different faces.
